code_analysis_tags.monitoring_evidence: No domain tests the >=28 nT/yr global-decay threshold. The single field-decay panel checks 77.0/77.0 at one station (raw-text/08-live-power.txt:228-230) — a different value, different scope, and a pred==obs identity rather than a live comparison.
code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: Geomagnetic dipole decay (~5%/century; ~15 nT/yr equatorial, ~21 nT/yr surface-averaged, Thebault et al. 2015 IGRF-12, doi:10.1186/s40623-015-0228-9) and SAA regional deepening are standard geomagnetism; the dome adopts the observations and renames the mechanism.
code_analysis_tags.post_hoc_evidence: Confirming values come from indexed public datasets (IGRF-14/WMM2025/INTERMAGNET) available at dome-commit time; no author-independent pre-registration located. Per c4: dome registered 2026-03-06, confirmed 2026-03-21 against 2024-2025 data — a 15-day prediction-to-confirmation cycle on already-published data.
code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: The >=28 nT/yr threshold is not derived from any dome-geometry equation; the dome field equation H(r)=8537*exp(-r/8619) yields no decay-rate prediction at all (it is a static altitude profile).

holes_found.description: Citation-support mismatch created by the ISS-2603 patch wording (the flaw is c4 own recommended text, applied verbatim by the decider — same authorship pattern c4 flagged for c3). The merged sentence now reads: the 28 nT/yr threshold is met at SAA-core stations on the long-run rate (the dome own regional confirmation cites ~30 nT over 14 months), though the dome own 14-month confirmation window annualizes to only 25.7 nT/yr — below the dome own 28 nT/yr threshold. The parenthetical offered in support of met on the long-run rate is the SAME ~30 nT/14-month figure the though-clause immediately shows failing the threshold (30*12/14=25.7<28). A defender can quote the sentence as self-undercutting: the reviewers say the threshold is met while their only in-line number shows it is not. The intended logic (multi-year long-run station rates exceed 28; the dome specific 14-month window does not) is sound but the in-line evidence no longer carries it.
holes_found.recommendation: Fold into the ISS-2618 rewrite (this sentence is inside its blast radius — do not micro-patch separately). Rewrite spec: support met at SAA-core stations on the long-run rate with a long-run source (INTERMAGNET/CHAOS-7 multi-year station rates, or the dome own station-table values once ISS-2618 re-extracts them), and keep the 14-month/25.7 arithmetic as a separate sentence attacking the dome confirmation window specifically.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome is pointing at a real phenomenon: SAA-region station decay rates genuinely are large (the dome station table cites -77 and -76 nT/yr values, per the c4 re-extract of /tmp/dome-fetched/02-wins.txt), far exceeding global-average rates — real spatial structure in secular variation (wins.json:WIN-042.detail_evidence, Thebault et al. 2015 citation).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: A regional extreme does not make the global claim (Global magnetic field decays at rate >=28 nT/year, wins.json:WIN-042.detail_claim) true — the global rate is ~15-21 nT/yr on either standard basis (doi:10.1186/s40623-015-0228-9) — and restating WIN-037 threshold arithmetic under a new WIN ID adds no independent confirmation (wins.json:WIN-042.tldr_verdict).
